speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: asked	the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources what preventive measures are in place to ensure that essential services are not affected by flash floods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: To this end, PUB has an island-wide drainage improvement programme to enhance the capacities of our drains and canals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: These pathway measures will ensure that our land and facilities for the essential services remain adequately protected against floods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: These source measures will improve the flexibility and adaptability of our drainage system to cope with higher intensity storms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: In particular, PUB sets higher platform and crest level requirements for critical installations, special facilities and developments with linkages to underground facilities, such as an underground MRT station.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: These measures will prevent flood waters from directly entering the facilities and causing disruption to essential services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Beyond structural enhancements, PUB has instituted measures to help the public, including essential service providers, better prepare for flash floods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: PUB has a network of about 200 water level sensors and 170 CCTVs installed to remotely monitor drain and flood conditions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: This information is freely available on PUB's website, social media platforms and mobile apps.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Since August 2011, PUB has also implemented a free SMS alert system to provide the public with early warnings of heavy rain and rising water levels in canals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Our holistic approach to flood management has served us well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: However, with climate change, we can expect to experience more extreme and unpredictable weather; from more frequent and intense storms, to longer and more severe dry spells.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: There is a fine balance we need to maintain in the face of climate change.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: PUB will continue to put in place measures to minimise flood risk on one hand and strengthen the drought resilience of our water supply on the other.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: My question actually arose because I read that there were certain reported cases of flash floods occurring near hospitals.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: One, have there been any known cases so far where essential services have been disrupted due to flooding?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Two, is there a protocol in place to inform emergency vehicles early on if their route has been affected by flooding?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Three, are there any measures which can be taken to minimise the need to divert emergency vehicles, as diversion may lead to time delays, if they have to go to another hospital?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I have gone through the records of the recent flash floods in the last couple of years and most of the flash floods receded within 30 minutes.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Obviously, that is not to say that we do not acknowledge the inconvenience and delay that might be caused.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But generally, whilst there might be delays or some cars might be stranded, public transport had not been affected – that means, buses and all that.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Even though there is a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for diversion, we have not had to do this for the incidents involved.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As to the question about known cases where emergency vehicles were delayed or diverted, I do not have information with regard to that.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Whether there is a protocol, PUB works very closely with LTA, SCDF and all the other agencies.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, once the Meteorological Services of Singapore (MSS) puts out an alert of a heavy storm, PUB's flood monitoring operations will kick in.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have said, we have got water sensors as well as CCTVs.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We also have access to LTA's CCTVs to monitor the situation and to give alerts in advance through social media websites, mobile apps, as well as on our PUB website.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: There is also a free SMS alert system.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: SCDF services would also utilise this to make sure that if there are any issues about flash floods in various areas, they will be aware of it.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Can the hon Member remind me what was the third question?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: The third question is: what are the measures which can be taken to minimise the need to divert emergency vehicles, as diversion may lead to more time delays?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Actually, the flood monitoring operations kick in and there is an operations centre.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, the public can also use our PUB-One hotline to inform us of any flash flood incidents that they may be aware of and, in the spirit of the Minister of State Mr Sam Tan, let me publicise PUB-One's hotline, too.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It is just "1800 Call PUB" or 1800 2255782.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It could be that there might be some ambulances which decided, because of the warnings that we had, to take a different route.
